paper_title: Enhancement of the Photoresponse in Organic Field-Effect Transistors by Incorporating Thin DNA Layers

qa_pairs.question: What material is utilized as the active organic semiconductor in the organic phototransistors described in this study?
qa_pairs.answer: PCBDR is the active organic semiconductor material used in the fabrication of the organic phototransistors.
qa_pairs.source_title: Enhancement of the Photoresponse in Organic Field-Effect Transistors by Incorporating Thin DNA Layers

qa_pairs.question: Which specific photoelectrons are tracked during X-ray photoemission spectroscopy (XPS) to verify the integration of DNA into PCBDR films?
qa_pairs.answer: The presence of DNA is confirmed by detecting P 2p and Na 1s photoelectrons, which represent the phosphorus in the DNA backbone and the sodium counter-ions, respectively.
qa_pairs.source_title: Enhancement of the Photoresponse in Organic Field-Effect Transistors by Incorporating Thin DNA Layers

qa_pairs.question: How does the incorporation of a DNA layer affect the electrical switching parameters of PCBDR-based OFETs relative to the electrode work function?
qa_pairs.answer: The DNA layer shifts the threshold voltage (Vth) and turn-on voltage (Von) of the PCBDR-based OFETs. These shifts are specifically dependent on the work function of the source-drain electrodes used, such as Au or Al.
qa_pairs.source_title: Enhancement of the Photoresponse in Organic Field-Effect Transistors by Incorporating Thin DNA Layers

qa_pairs.question: What is the effect of the thin DNA layer on the bulk optical absorption properties of the PCBDR semiconductor film?
qa_pairs.answer: The incorporation of the thin DNA layer does not significantly alter the optical absorption properties, as the steady-state absorbance spectra of PCBDR and PCBDR/DNA films remain very similar.
qa_pairs.source_title: Enhancement of the Photoresponse in Organic Field-Effect Transistors by Incorporating Thin DNA Layers

qa_pairs.question: What are the specific device dimensions and operating voltages used to characterize the PCBDR/DNA OFETs in the linear regime?
qa_pairs.answer: The devices feature a channel width (Wch) of 1 mm and a channel length (Lch) of 70 μm. They are characterized in the linear regime using a drain voltage (Vd) of 12 V and a gate voltage (Vg) up to 60 V.
qa_pairs.source_title: Enhancement of the Photoresponse in Organic Field-Effect Transistors by Incorporating Thin DNA Layers

qa_pairs.question: Which characterization technique was employed to determine the work function of the Au and Al electrodes used in the phototransistors?
qa_pairs.answer: Scanning Kelvin probe microscopy was used to determine the work function (WF) of the metal electrodes.
qa_pairs.source_title: Enhancement of the Photoresponse in Organic Field-Effect Transistors by Incorporating Thin DNA Layers

qa_pairs.question: How does the performance of PCBDR/DNA devices under illumination compare to their performance in dark conditions?
qa_pairs.answer: The PCBDR/DNA devices show a significant enhancement in drain current under illumination compared to dark conditions, indicating a substantial improvement in the photoresponse due to the DNA layer.
qa_pairs.source_title: Enhancement of the Photoresponse in Organic Field-Effect Transistors by Incorporating Thin DNA Layers

qa_pairs.question: What was the purpose of applying a DC voltage (Vdc) of -0.28 V during Electrostatic Force Microscopy (EFM) measurements of the films?
qa_pairs.answer: The Vdc of -0.28 V was applied during 1ω EFM measurements to cancel out the contact potential difference between the tip and the sample surface for both PCBDR and PCBDR/DNA films.
qa_pairs.source_title: Enhancement of the Photoresponse in Organic Field-Effect Transistors by Incorporating Thin DNA Layers
